subject: Dasouki et al. (2013)
object: Dasouki et al. (2013) reported 2 siblings from a Micronesian family with idiopathic autosomal recessive aplastic anemia. Both parents and a sibling who were heterozygous carriers had reduced platelet counts, whereas a sibling with wildtype sequence had a normal platelet count.

subject: Dasouki et al. (2013)
object: In 2 Micronesian sibs with autosomal recessive aplastic anemia, Dasouki et al. (2013) identified by whole-exome sequencing a homozygous c.112C>T mutation in the THPO gene, resulting in an arg38-to-cys (R38C) substitution, or R17C excluding the 21-amino acid signal peptide, in the receptor-binding domain. In silico modeling predicted that the introduced fifth cysteine may disrupt normal disulfide bonding among the 4 conserved RBD cysteines and impair receptor binding. Mutant THPO-containing media showed a 2- to 3-fold reduced ability to sustain proliferation of THPO-dependent UT7-TPO cells, and the authors concluded that R17C is a partial loss-of-function allele causing aplastic anemia in the homozygous state and mild thrombocytopenia in the heterozygous state.

subject: Dasouki et al. (2013)
object: Dasouki et al. (2013) found that the THPO R17C partial loss-of-function allele resulted in aplastic anemia in the homozygous state and mild thrombocytopenia in the heterozygous state in their family.

subject: Seo et al. (2017)
object: Seo et al. (2017) reported 5 individuals from 3 unrelated families with severe thrombocytopenia that progressed to trilineage bone marrow failure. Four of the children received hematopoietic stem cell transplants. All 4 had poor graft function and persistent severe cytopenias, even after repeated transplants from different donors.

subject: Seo et al. (2017)
object: Seo et al. (2017) used exome and targeted sequencing to identify a homozygous R99W mutation in the THPO gene in affected children from 2 of the 3 families with thrombocytopenia progressing to bone marrow failure. The mutation resulted in a lack of THPO in the patients' serum.

subject: Seo et al. (2017)
object: Seo et al. (2017) identified a homozygous R157X nonsense mutation in the THPO gene in the affected child in a third family with thrombocytopenia progressing to bone marrow failure. The patient had no THPO in the serum.

subject: Seo et al. (2017)
object: Seo et al. (2017) concluded that biallelic loss-of-function mutations in THPO cause bone marrow failure. They proposed that the bone marrow failure does not respond to transplant because the mechanism lies outside the hematopoietic cells. They stated that this supports the critical role of the MPL-THPO pathway in hematopoiesis.

subject: Seo et al. (2017)
object: Seo et al. (2017) found that THPO was absent from the serum of patients carrying either the R99W or the R157X mutation.

subject: Seo et al. (2017)
object: Seo et al. (2017) reported that the 2 surviving patients showed improvement in trilineage hematopoiesis after treatment with a THPO receptor agonist.

subject: Pecci et al. (2018)
object: Pecci et al. (2018) reported 3 sibs with congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia, born to first-cousin Egyptian parents. The proband, a boy, presented at 3.5 years of age with ecchymoses. He had very severe thrombocytopenia (platelets 3 x 10(9)/l), hyporegenerative anemia and severe neutropenia. Bone marrow was hypocellular with very rare immature megakaryocytes and a normal karyotype. He also had preauricular skin tags and a left divergent squint. He was initially diagnosed with idiopathic aplastic anemia, after Fanconi anemia and PNH were excluded. He went on to have recurrent major hemorrhages and severe infections that required multiple transfusions.

subject: Pecci et al. (2018)
object: Pecci et al. (2018) found that the proband's brother had severe isolated thrombocytopenia (26 x 10(9)/l) at 7 months of age, with markedly reduced bone marrow megakaryocytes. He developed recurrent spontaneous bleeding at 1.6 years. A younger sister developed a hematoma at a vaccination site at 2 months of age and was found to have anemia and severe thrombocytopenia. Platelet size and blood cell morphology were normal. The authors noted that the oldest sib had trilineage hypoplasia, which suggested that the hematologic picture worsens with age, and that the phenotype was indistinguishable from CAMT caused by MPL mutations.

subject: Pecci et al. (2018)
object: Pecci et al. (2018) sequenced MPL and THPO in the proband and found no MPL variants. They identified a homozygous c.355C>T variant in THPO (p.R119C). The variant segregated with the disease: both affected sibs were homozygous and the parents were heterozygous. It was absent from the dbSNP, 1000 Genomes and ExAC databases, and most in silico tools predicted it to be pathogenic.

subject: Pecci et al. (2018)
object: Pecci et al. (2018) studied the R119C mutant in transfected HEK293T cells. It was expressed at levels similar to or higher than wildtype and was equally stable, but its concentration in culture supernatants was about 23-fold lower, indicating impaired secretion. When tested at equal concentrations, the mutant had about 50% of wildtype activity in stimulating proliferation of THPO-dependent UT7-TPO cells and in activating STAT5, ERK1/2 and AKT. The previously reported R38C mutant behaved similarly.

subject: Pecci et al. (2018)
object: Pecci et al. (2018) found normal serum THPO levels in the 2 older affected sibs before treatment: 10.9 pg/ml in the proband and 14.1 pg/ml in his brother, compared with 6.9 to 54.4 pg/ml in controls. Serum THPO is markedly elevated in other forms of marrow aplasia, including MPL-related CAMT, so these levels were inappropriately low. The authors suggested that measuring serum THPO could help distinguish THPO-related CAMT from MPL-related CAMT.

subject: Pecci et al. (2018)
object: Pecci et al. (2018) reported that the proband had not responded to cyclosporine A or oxymetholone. He was started on romiplostim at 4.4 years of age and showed a rapid trilineage response, with no further bleeding, infections or transfusions over 6.5 years of follow-up. Both sibs also responded to romiplostim. The brother achieved platelet counts of 30 to 100 x 10(9)/l and transfusion independence over 6.3 years. The authors noted that hematopoietic stem cell transplantation is not expected to be effective in patients with THPO mutations.

subject: Capaci et al. (2023)
object: Capaci et al. (2023) reported a boy born to consanguineous Muslim Palestinian parents (first cousins) who came to medical attention at 3.5 years with easy bruising and thrombocytopenia (21 x 10(9)/L) and a normal mean platelet volume. His platelet count shortly after birth was 70 x 10(9)/L. At age 2 years he had severe thrombocytopenia (20 x 10(9)/L) when diagnosed with urethral stenosis. Bone marrow examination showed normocellular marrow with severe megakaryocyte hypoplasia and mild dyserythropoiesis; aside from mild occasional neutropenia he had no other cytopenias, and Fanconi anemia was excluded by chromosomal breakage analysis.

subject: Capaci et al. (2023)
object: By whole-exome sequencing in the Palestinian boy with CAMT, Capaci et al. (2023) identified a homozygous c.-323C>T substitution (chr3:g.184096040G>A, GRCh37) in the promoter region of the THPO gene (transcript variant 1, NM_000460), 45 nucleotides upstream of the transcription start site. The parents and a younger sibling were heterozygous and two healthy siblings were homozygous wildtype; the variant was in dbSNP (rs1208732776) but not in gnomAD, and lies in a region conserved across species. No variants were found in MPL, MECOM, HOXA11, RBM8A or other bone marrow failure genes.

subject: Capaci et al. (2023)
object: Capaci et al. (2023) noted that the heterozygous mother and younger sibling of the homozygous proband had asymptomatic mild thrombocytopenia (mother around 80 x 10(9)/L, worsening during pregnancies; sibling 130 x 10(9)/L at birth), consistent with mild thrombocytopenia in carriers of monoallelic THPO loss-of-function variants.

subject: Capaci et al. (2023)
object: Capaci et al. (2023) found that c.-323C>T lies within predicted ETS1 and STAT4 binding sites that were abolished by the variant. In luciferase assays in HEK293T cells the mutant THPO promoter reduced reporter activity by almost 80%; silencing ETS1 and/or STAT4 reduced wildtype promoter activity, and chromatin immunoprecipitation showed reduced binding of the transcription factors, at least STAT4, to the mutant promoter.

subject: Capaci et al. (2023)
object: Capaci et al. (2023) showed that knockdown of ETS1 and STAT4 in HepG2 hepatocyte cells strongly reduced endogenous THPO mRNA and protein, and that ETS1 and STAT4 interact (proximity ligation and coimmunoprecipitation), suggesting they form a transcriptional complex on THPO regulatory sequences. STAT3 knockdown also reduced THPO expression, although no STAT3 binding site was predicted in the promoter.

subject: Capaci et al. (2023)
object: Capaci et al. (2023) found that the proband's serum THPO concentration was 126 pg/mL (reference 15-80 pg/mL for children), only slightly elevated despite the severely reduced megakaryocyte and platelet mass, whereas THPO levels are expected to be markedly elevated in amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia (median 1,493 pg/mL in 56 patients with CAMT due to MPL mutations). The authors suggested that a normal serum THPO in amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia should prompt suspicion of a THPO defect.

subject: Capaci et al. (2023)
object: Capaci et al. (2023) treated the proband with eltrombopag, starting at 1.4 mg/kg/day; platelet count stabilized around 40 x 10(9)/L after 1 month, and after a dose increase to 2.8 mg/kg/day it rose gradually to 125 x 10(9)/L after 6 months, with resolution of easy bruising. This was the first report of eltrombopag therapy in a patient with a THPO mutation.
